title: RBAC v2 canary cutover, automated fallbacks, and audit preservation runbook
creator: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:
This ticket contains an operational runbook and acceptance criteria for executing a staged migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 across hosted and dedicated environments. The runbook emphasizes: (1) audit log preservation and immutability guarantees during cutover, (2) deterministic dual-write with idempotent backfills, (3) canary cohorts for SSO/SAML-mapped orgs and admin controls, and (4) automated fallback/rollback triggers and communication triggers to customers and support.

Goals:
- Preserve audit integrity: every authz decision and role mapping change must be recorded to immutable audit buckets with a tamper-evident checksum.
- Enable safe dual-write: live traffic should write to v1 and v2 with monotonic reconciliation and idempotent backfill jobs.
- Minimize customer disruption via canaries and per-org opt-out controls.
- Provide clear rollback criteria and automated fallback path to RBAC v1 for affected orgs.

Out of scope:
- Full UI redesign for role-management (handled in DES/PM tickets).
- Long-term analytics migration (>90 days) — separate archival migration will follow.

Operational constraints and assumptions:
- Customers using custom SAML assertions may require targeted mapping validation before cutover.
- Dedicated clusters can be scheduled independently; hosted customers follow global rollout windows.
- Backfill jobs are rate-limited by a per-cluster throttle to avoid OOM/IO spikes.

Runbook steps (high level):
1) Pre-cutover validation (2 weeks before):
   - Inventory orgs by SSO type and custom claim usage via query: SELECT org_id, sso_type, custom_claims FROM identity.orgs WHERE updated_at > now() - interval '90 days';
   - Run dry-run of mapping logic against 10k random users and fail if >0.1% unexpected role changes.
   - Snapshot RBAC v1 state (roles, bindings, admin flags) to immutable storage with SHA256 manifest.
2) Enable dual-write (day -1):
   - Deploy feature flag rbac_v2_dualwrite=true (per-region rollout).
   - Partial traffic test: 1% of requests mirror to v2 but continue reading from v1. Verify latency SLO impact <15ms median.
3) Start idempotent backfill (day 0..N):
   - Launch backfill jobs in 15-minute windows per cluster; each job writes a transaction log entry and idempotency token.
   - Maintain job-level checkpoints in migration.checkpoints table for resumability.
4) Canary cutover (day +2..+7):
   - Select canary cohort: 3% orgs weighted by size and SSO sophistication (include SSO, OIDC, and non-SSO).
   - For each canary org: enable v2 reads; keep writes dual-written. Monitor for authentication failures and permission mismatches.
   - Hold canary for 72 hours minimum with automated verification.
5) Progressive rollout and reconciliation (after successful canary):
   - Expand cohorts to 10%, 30%, 60%, 100% with 48-72h stabilization windows.
   - Run nightly reconciliation job that produces delta reports; deltas >0.05% for any org creates auto-ticket and halts expansion.
6) Cutover completion and deprecation (post-100%):
   - Flip global read to v2 and continue writes for 24h.
   - After 7 days of stable telemetry, schedule v1 write retirement.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- Dashboards must show: per-org permission mismatch rate, auth failure rate, median latency by route, backfill progress by shard, and audit upload success/failure.
- Critical alerts: permission_mismatch_rate > 0.2% for 5m, auth_failure_rate > 1% baseline + 0.5% absolute, reconciliation_job_error_rate > 0.5%.

Rollback & fallback strategy:
- Per-org rollback via feature flag: rbac_v2_read=off for the org. This immediately routes reads back to v1 while preserving v2 writes for postmortem.
- Global rollback: if systemic regression (latency spike >50ms median or platform-wide auth failure >2%), flip rbac_v2_dualwrite=false and route all writes to v1.
- All rollbacks must be executed through the control-plane runbook with operator-confirmation steps and customer notification templates.

Audit preservation details:
- All RBAC changes and decision logs are exported as newline-delimited JSON to an immutable S3/GCS bucket with object-level write-once policy and periodic snapshot manifests.
- Each exported object contains: timestamp, actor_id, org_id, request_id, decision, prior_binding_snapshot_sha256.
- Compliance requirement: preserve chain-of-custody index accessible to Security and Customer Success for 90 days.

Customer communication and support flow:
- Pre-cutover notice: 2 weeks, include list of affected features and devtips for SSO claim checks.
- Canary invite: opt-in link for teams wanting early migration and a known rollback SLA.
- Incident comms: templated emails and status page snippets ready for severity P0/P1.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backfill completes for 99% of users within defined window without causing >5% CPU increase on control-plane clusters.
- Canary cohort shows permission mismatch rate below 0.05% for 72 hours.
- Audit export manifests show no missing sequence numbers and pass manifest SHA256 verification.
- Feature flags and per-org fallbacks are operational and tested via automated e2e test harness.

Deliverables and artifacts: see artifacts list below for links to the detailed plan, migration scripts, and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria:
- 99% backfill success within allotted migration window.
- Permission mismatch rate <0.05% for canaries over 72h.
- Audit manifests verifiable via SHA256 and chain-of-custody queries.
- Per-org rollback exercised in staging and demonstrated within 5 minutes.
- Automated reconciliation generates delta reports and creates tickets when thresholds exceeded.
updates: 2026-01-12: Ticket created by Maya Patel, initial draft runbook attached.
2026-01-20: Security review kickoff — Zoe Kim and Priya Singh reviewed audit bucket immutability approach; recommended adding manifest SHA256 verification (actioned).

2026-02-02: Engineering spike completed: dual-write proxy implemented with idempotency tokens. Performance tests show median +8ms in worst-case for mirrored writes. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/4123
2026-02-18: SRE run simulated backfill in staging with 10k orgs; observed reconciliation deltas at 0.03%. Increased per-shard throttle to reduce transient IO.
2026-02-25: PM approved canary cohorts and customer comms draft. Customer success provided list of 40 orgs willing to opt-in to early migration.
2026-03-01: Dry-run of per-org rollback executed in staging; rollback completed in 3m42s end-to-end (target <5m).
2026-03-05: Observability owners (Liam O'Connor) published dashboard templates. Added alert runbooks to ops playbook.
2026-03-12: Final sign-off meeting with Security, SRE, PM. Scheduled first canary rollout for 2026-03-22.
rollback_criteria: Per-org rollback if permission_mismatch_rate > 0.2% for 30m or if customer reports a P0 auth-breaking issue. Global rollback if platform auth_failure_rate > 2% for 10m or median route latency increases by >50ms for more than 15m.
monitoring_signals:
- permission_mismatch_rate (per-org, per-region)
- auth_failure_rate (by route)
- backfill_job_success_ratio
- reconciliation_delta_rate
- audit_export_success_rate
- median and p95 latency by endpoint
notes: Operator tips: use staging-runbook script to generate a simulated audit export and validate manifest verification locally. Make sure to coordinate with Customer Success before enabling canary for any org listed as high-touch. All actions must be timestamped and include operator_id in the control-plane audit log.
